claims.text: An active-learning machine-learned interatomic potential trained on solid and liquid ab initio MD configurations can substitute for explicit AIMD or TOR-TILD sampling near fusion.
Active learning can tailor an MLP training set to the relevant configurational space while minimizing the required DFT calculations.
ML potentials can attain accuracy near that of their underlying DFT calculations in elemental and multicomponent systems.
The proposed workflow will iteratively train on DFT configurations from both solid and liquid states over 0.8–1.0 Tm.
The trained MLP will be used for thermodynamic integration to calculate phase free energies and fusion properties.
The method is applicable first to elemental Fe and can be extended to the multicomponent CoCrFeNi alloy.
The MLP will preserve critical local vibrational modes and anharmonic fluctuations through its refined training set.
The MLP will preserve electron–vibration coupling effects through its training set.
Iterative active learning can capture the full configurational ensembles of both solid and liquid states.
Replacing direct AIMD sampling with the actively learned potential enables rapid sampling of free-energy surfaces.
On-the-fly DFT corrections ensure that high-entropy effects and delicate entropy contributions are maintained.
The workflow will reduce computational cost by approximately one order of magnitude relative to explicit AIMD or TOR-TILD.
The workflow will produce free energies within approximately 5% of explicit AIMD or TOR-TILD results.
Free-energy fidelity within 5% is sufficient to reliably predict fusion properties and associated thermodynamic observables.
The method is expected to remain reliable over 0.8–1.0 Tm.
Failure to include rare but critical configurations can reduce MLP reliability.
Subtle electron–vibration coupling and anharmonic effects in highly multicomponent systems may cause errors exceeding 5%.
A difference greater than approximately 5% in phase free energies or derived observables relative to explicit AIMD or TOR-TILD would falsify the hypothesis.
